body.statement: For every fixed finite collection of independent empirical distribution functions based on independent and identically distributed cell samples, the centered root-sample-size empirical processes converge jointly to independent Brownian bridges composed with their cell distribution functions.  At finitely many atoms, evaluation gives a centered Gaussian vector with covariance \(\min(c_r,c_{r'})-c_rc_{r'}\) within a cell and zero covariance across cells.

source.locator: Section 2.1 and Theorem 2.5.2, specialized to the distribution-function indicator class and a fixed finite product
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2.5.2. Let F be a class of measurable functions that satisfies the uniform entropy bound (2.5.1). Let the classes F_delta = {f - g: f, g in F, ||f - g||_(P,2) < delta} and F_delta^2 be P-measurable for every delta > 0. If P*F^2 < infinity, then F is P-Donsker.

attestation.note: Direct transcription from van der Vaart and Wellner (1996), p. 127, in the National Academic Digital Library of Ethiopia public repository scan at https://ndl.ethernet.edu.et/handle/123456789/26495; applied to the distribution-function indicator class, then to the fixed finite independent product.
